article_title: Confirming Correct, Missing the Rest: LLM Tutoring Agents Struggle Where Feedback Matters Most
citation: Tahreem Yasir, Wenbo Li, Sam Gilson, Sutapa Dey Tithi, Xiaoyi Tian, Tiffany Barnes. (2026). Confirming Correct, Missing the Rest: LLM Tutoring Agents Struggle Where Feedback Matters Most. arXiv:2605.16207. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16207
title: KG-grounded benchmark of 10,836 solution-feedback pairs for step-level LLM tutoring evaluation
description: The article introduces what it calls "the first benchmark for step-level evaluation of LLM tutoring feedback across multiple valid solution paths." It is built from 516 unique proof states drawn from 32 proof problems across five practice levels of a propositional logic tutor deployed in an undergraduate Discrete Mathematics course, with LLM-simulated next-step solutions and reasoning traces. The article reports that "we evaluate 10,836 LLM- simulated next-step solutions and their feedback with KG-grounded evaluation across seven mod- els and three feedback conditions." Code and data are released in a public repository.
requirements: LLM-simulated student solutions with reasoning traces, because the tutoring system logs lack reasoning traces needed for step-level reasoning evaluation
constraints: Proof states come from a single undergraduate Discrete Mathematics course at one institution, which the authors state limits the diversity of reasoning contexts and problem types
target_learning_goals: step-level propositional logic proof diagnosis and feedback evaluation
examples: Each of seven models served as both student simulator generating solutions for all 516 proof states and feedback agent evaluating all solutions under three conditions
key_sources: Tahreem Yasir, Wenbo Li, Sam Gilson, Sutapa Dey Tithi, Xiaoyi Tian, Tiffany Barnes. (2026). Confirming Correct, Missing the Rest: LLM Tutoring Agents Struggle Where Feedback Matters Most. arXiv:2605.16207. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16207

article_title: Multi-source Education Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion for College Curricula
citation: Zeju Li, Linya Cheng, Chunhong Zhang, Xinning Zhu, Hui Zhao. (2023). Multi-source Education Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion for College Curricula. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.04567
title: Four-part knowledge graph fusion preserving hierarchy, attributes and edges
description: The article's fusion method integrates fragmentary nodes referring to the same knowledge concept across sources while retaining information content. It proceeds in four parts: "entity name matching, locating coarse-grained entities, attribute union, and preserving original edges". The fused node is placed at the coarsest granularity level, attributes (except url) are unioned, and all pre-fusion connection relationships are reconnected to the unique fused node. Fusion is applied both within a course across sources and between courses.
requirements: Entity name matching using string matching, literal similarity and semantic similarity to determine whether entities refer to the same concept
constraints: The fused node is located at the coarsest level of the entities fused, which the authors state preserves the hierarchical structure
target_learning_goals: integrating distributed knowledge concepts into a unified knowledge base
examples: Two 'anti-noise performance' nodes were fused into one node retaining the union of name, description, word frequency and ranker attributes
key_sources: Zeju Li, Linya Cheng, Chunhong Zhang, Xinning Zhu, Hui Zhao. (2023). Multi-source Education Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion for College Curricula. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.04567
